_comment: Optimizely.Performance.Counters - settings template for CMS 12 and CMS 13.
Merge the 'Optimizely' block below into your site's appsettings.json. Every value shown is
the default, so a site that copies this file wholesale behaves exactly as it does with no
configuration at all - delete the lines you are not changing.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored. Anything else the package
does not recognise is logged as a warning at startup, so a typo is visible rather than silent.
This is a different section from Optimizely:PerformanceCounters, which belongs to
Optimizely.Performance.DotNetCounters. The two packages are usually installed together and
configured separately.

_comment_Enabled: The master switch. False and nothing is decorated, no probe starts and no counter is
registered with Application Insights - the modules log one line each and return. It is
here so that an operator suspecting this package during an incident can rule it out with
a setting rather than a deployment.

_comment: The four probes measure conditions nothing publishes a counter for. Each can be turned
off on its own. GarbageCollection and Contention need .NET 6 or later and never run on
CMS 11 whatever they are set to; CacheLock finds nothing on CMS 11 for the same reason
the cascade counters are absent there.

ThreadPool._comment_SampleIntervalSeconds: Each sample is one queued work item.
ThreadPool._comment_SampleTimeoutSeconds: A sample that does not finish inside this is recorded as starvation.
ThreadPool._comment_SlowSampleThresholdMilliseconds: Delay above which a sample is also logged.

GarbageCollection._comment_SlowPauseThresholdMilliseconds: Pause above which a sample is also logged.

_comment_BurstCaptureEnabled: False leaves the contention rate running and stops the short capture bursts that
measure how long the waits were. The rate is the free half of the probe.
_comment_BurstTriggerContentionsPerSecon: Contention is normal and a busy site produces a steady background rate. The default
sits well above it, so a burst means something changed.

_comment_Enabled: The switch for the only reflection over Optimizely internals in the package. False
loses the four Optimizely.CMS.Cache.Lock* counters and nothing else.
CacheLock._comment_QueueDepthThreshold: Total queue depth above which a sample is logged. Zero silences the log.

_comment_Enabled: False leaves IMemoryCache undecorated, which removes the cost as well as the nine
cascade counters. Cache hit, miss and invalidation rates are measured a layer up and
are unaffected. Has no effect on CMS 11, which has no IMemoryCache under its object
_comment_LargeRemovalThreshold: A counter cannot carry a cache key, so a cascade this size or larger is also written
to the log, naming the key responsible. That is the only way to find out which key is
Cascade._comment_FailureThreshold: Consecutive failures after which the recorder switches itself off for the process.

_comment: The log write rate counters. Not under Probes, because this is not a probe: a probe
looks on its own thread, and this counts on whichever thread wrote the log entry.
On CMS 12 and CMS 13 the counting is done by an ILoggerProvider named
OptimizelyLogWriteRate, which sees every write the host's logging dispatches. It counts
at the host's default minimum level; to widen what it sees without changing what any
real sink writes, set Logging:OptimizelyLogWriteRate:LogLevel:Default in the standard
ASP.NET Core logging section. On CMS 11 the same counters come from a log4net appender
instead and this switch controls both.
False loses the three Optimizely.Runtime.Logging.* counters and nothing else. The
provider is then not registered at all, so it costs the site nothing.
